newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KLINSMANN APOLOGISES FOR YELLING AT COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KLINSMANN APOLOGISES FOR YELLING AT COACH.

text.p: Bayern Munich striker Juergen Klinsmann has apologised for yelling at coach Giovanni Trapattoni and kicking a hole in an advertisement sign after being substituted in the 0-0 draw with Freiburg on Saturday.
"A lot of things were boiling up inside me...and I had to swallow a lot," Klinsmann said. "It was an over-reaction, something that should not happen to an experienced player."
Trapattoni replaced Germany captain Klinsmann with Carsten Lakies. It was the 12th time this season that he had been substituted during a match.
"He said excuse me mister, that was a mistake," Trappattoni said. "I have taken out many great players. I am not God but I have 20 years experience."
When he came off Klinsmann kicked a hole in a five-millimetre thick wooden advertising sign on the sidelines.
"I wanted to leave Munich with them as champions," said Klinsmann who is leaving the club at the end of the season. "But we are slowly running into the danger that that won't happen."
Second-placed Bayer Leverkusen were playing Hamburg on Sunday. A win would take them to within one point of the leaders.
Bayern president Franz Beckenbauer said the match against bottom club Freiburg was embarrassing.
"One can only laugh after this performance," he said. "In this form we have zero chance of winning the championship."
